inRowSpacingIn.publisher: University of Maryland Extension, Home and Garden Information Center
inRowSpacingIn.quote: UMD HGIC, Growing Winter Squash in a Home Garden: "Spacing: Seeds should be planted every 3 ft. to 4 ft. apart in rows that are about 6 to 8 feet apart, depending on the type."
inRowSpacingIn.note: VCE is internally inconsistent (426-331 Table 5: Squash, winter 2-4 ft; 426-406: bush 3-4 ft, semi-vining 4-6 ft, vining 5-7 ft), so the UMD figure, which overlaps both, is used.

keepApart.publisher: University of Wisconsin-Madison Division of Extension, Garden Facts XHT1132 (David M. Lowenstein and Russell L. Groves, "Potato Leafhopper")
keepApart.quote: Avoid planting sensitive crops near alfalfa fields , because PLHs will migrate from alfalfa to these crops when the alfalfa field is harvested.
keepApart.note: The same fact sheet names the sensitive crops: "Snap beans and potatoes should be monitored regularly for PLH activity , especially in early summer after alfalfa is cut." Only snap bean (Phaseolus vulgaris pod bean) and potato plugins are listed; other PLH hosts the sheet mentions (eggplant, strawberry, apple) are not tied to the alfalfa advice there. Michigan State Extension E-2269 (1992) agrees for dry beans: "Be sure to check dry bean fields after nearby alfalfa fields are cut because cutting causes the adult leafhoppers to leave alfalfa fields." The spacing before "PLH" and "," is as extracted from the PDF text.

seedingRate.drillRowSpacingIn.publisher: Virginia Cooperative Extension, Agronomy Handbook 2023 (424-100), Part I, Wheat
seedingRate.drillRowSpacingIn.quote: Plant 120-150 lbs per acre (36 seeds per sq ft or 20 seeds per drill foot in 7-inch rows). Plant in 6-8 inch rows or solid-seeded.
seedingRate.drillRowSpacingIn.note: The October 2004 VCE Crop and Soil Environmental News wheat seeding article also tables 6, 7 and 8 inch rows. The same sentence sources the drilled lb rate.

seedingRate.drilledLbsPerAcre.publisher: Virginia Cooperative Extension, Agronomy Handbook 2023 (424-100), Part I, Wheat
seedingRate.drilledLbsPerAcre.quote: Plant 120-150 lbs per acre (36 seeds per sq ft or 20 seeds per drill foot in 7-inch rows). Plant in 6-8 inch rows or solid-seeded.
seedingRate.drilledLbsPerAcre.note: Counted as a drilled rate (panel ruling 2026-10-05, #551, 2-1): restated per drill foot in 7-inch rows. Missouri G4652's drilled 90-100 is a forage pure-stand rate and does not count for a grain plugin. Seeds per sq ft stay empty: 36 here vs 30-35 in the October 2004 VCE Crop and Soil Environmental News article, the October 2015 Virginia Ag Pest and Crop Advisory ('a seeding rate of 30-35 seeds per square foot') and Kentucky AGR-18 (no overlap, permanent until a source changes).

seedDepthIn.publisher: SARE, Managing Cover Crops Profitably 3rd ed., Winter Wheat
seedDepthIn.quote: Drill 60 to 120 lb./A (1 to 2 bushels) into a firm seedbed at a 1/2- to 11/2-inch depth
seedDepthIn.note: Seed depth, sourced panel ruling 2026-10-05, #551; the source-coverage gate does not check this field. The web text prints '11/2' for 1 1/2 (Chart 3B's wheat row: 1/2–1 1/2). Was 1-1.5 (unsourced); PA NRCS 340 winter wheat 1.0-1.5 overlaps. VCE 424-100 gives no depth.

harvestIndicators.publisher: Sustainable Agriculture Research and Education (SARE, USDA NIFA), Managing Cover Crops Profitably, 3rd Edition
harvestIndicators.quote: SARE, Managing Cover Crops Profitably, White Clover, Killing White Clover Cover Crops: "Thorough uprooting and incorporation by chisel or moldboard plowing, field cultivating, undercutting or rotary tilling, or—in spring—use of a suitable herbicide will result in good to excellent kill of white clover. Extremely close mowing and partial tillage that leaves any roots undisturbed will suppress, but not kill, white clover."

seedingRate.drilledLbsPerAcre.publisher: University of Missouri Extension G4652, Seeding Rates, Dates and Depths for Common Missouri Forages (Harley D. Naumann)
seedingRate.drilledLbsPerAcre.quote: Missouri G4652 Table 1. Pure stands, columns "Type | Seeding rate (pounds of live seed per acre) | Seeding date (Spring, Fall, Dormant or frost seeding) | Depth"; row "Timothy Perennial, cool-season grass Drilled: 4 – 6 Broadcast: 8 – 10 February – March Mid-August – early September 1/4 – 1/2 inch"
seedingRate.drilledLbsPerAcre.note: Forage pure-stand rate; the plugin is a hay timothy, so it counts (panel ruling 2026-10-05, #551). Kentucky AGR-84 Timothy, the crop guide, gives the same 'plant at the rate of 4 to 6 lb of seed per acre' for pure stands, in the paragraph on tilled seedbeds and no-till drilling. VCE 424-100 ('8-10 lbs alone'), Kentucky AGR-18 and Tennessee give 8-10 or 8 with no method, so they do not count. Missouri says 'live seed' but not 'pure live seed', so no seedBasis is set.

seedingRate.broadcastLbsPerAcre.quote: Missouri G4652 Table 1. seedingRate.drillRowSpacingIn.quote: Any no-till drill that plants in 7-inch to 8-inch rows and is set to deliver seed at the proper rate and depth will produce high yielding stands of timothy with only one pass across a field.
seedingRate.drillRowSpacingIn.note: Crop guide; single source for the drill row width (panel ruling 2026-10-05, #551, 3-0).

seedingRate.broadcastLbsPerAcre.publisher: USDA NRCS Plant Guide, Japanese millet (Echinochloa esculenta)
seedingRate.broadcastLbsPerAcre.quote: It can be broadcast at 20 lb/ac and covered lightly ¼ in deep for wildlife food planting (Stewart and West, 2004) or directly seeded into mud flats or well-prepared fields.
seedingRate.broadcastLbsPerAcre.note: Crop guide's single figure; UGA C814 (broadcast 20-25) and Kentucky AGR-18 ('20 lb (broadcast)', pure live seed) contain it (panel ruling 2026-10-05, #551, 3-0). The guide's '20–25 lb/ac' names no method. Drilled stays empty: UGA C814 15-20, AGR-18 10 and MD/PA NRCS 340 25 and 20 do not all overlap. NRCS Iowa (12/14) and Ohio ANR-0115 (12-15/14-17) are MCCC pure live seed baselines, not counted. No seed basis stated.

seedingRate.seedsPerAcre.publisher: University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension AGR-18, Grain, Forage, and Cover Crop Guide for Kentucky
seedingRate.seedsPerAcre.quote: Kentucky AGR-18 table, columns "Species Scientific Name | Uses | Common Units | Desired Plant Density | Seeding Rate Pure Live Seed/ac | Seeding Depth (inches)"; row "Sorghum, Grain (Milo) Sorghum bicolor | grain | 56 lb/bu 24,000 seeds/lb | 60,000/ac | 60,000 to 80,000 seeds | 3/4 to 1-1/4"
seedingRate.seedsPerAcre.note: Row read from the PDF layout and written with its column names; 60,000/ac is the desired plant density, 60,000 to 80,000 the seeds planted. Single source; nothing disagrees (panel ruling 2026-10-05, #551, 3-0). The lb rate stays empty: VCE 424-100 'Plant for grain at 5-7 lbs in rows' (wide rows, not a drill) and UGA C814 D 6-8, and University of Delaware Weekly Crop Update (May 16, 2008) says 'Do not plant using the older suggestions of pounds per acre since grain sorghum seed size has varied from almost 8,000 seed per pound up to 18,000 seed per pound.' Row width stays empty: Delaware's 7-10 in and AGR-18's '15" or less' compare yield and lodging, they do not recommend a width.

seedingRate.notRecorded.publisher: University of Maryland Extension FS-1134, No-Till Spring Vegetables After Forage Radish Cover Crop
seedingRate.notRecorded.quote: Recommended seeding rates for the popular Tillage Radish brand are 6 lbs/acre drilled, though research trials at the University of Maryland generally used a higher seeding rate of 8-9 lbs/acre. Broadcast rates are higher (9-12 lbs/acre)
seedingRate.notRecorded.note: Why both rates are empty (panel ruling 2026-10-05, #551, 2-1): UMD's brand rate (6 drilled, 9-12 broadcast) does not overlap SARE's forage radish 8-12 drilled and shares only 12 with SARE's 12-20 broadcast; PA NRCS 340 says 5. The brand owner (DLF / La Crosse Seed) prints 'Seeding Rate - Alone/New (Lbs./Acre) 3-8' with no method, so it does not count.
